Pricing

Three plans, sized to the operational scale of your supply chain.

All plans include the Lattice & Spire data model, supplier 360 master record, certified ERP integrations, and an annual platform release cadence. Pricing scales with spend under management and the number of active integrations.

Essentials

For mid-market industrials operationalizing supplier visibility for the first time.

Pricing FAQ

Questions we get asked the most.

How is pricing calculated?
Pricing scales with three primary inputs: spend under management, the number of certified integrations, and the count of named users. Add-on modules (ESG Tracker, additional Forecast Engine categories, tier-3 Network Graph) are licensed independently. Quoted ranges are typical; final pricing is delivered as a defended proposal.
Is there a minimum contract term?
All plans are annual contracts at minimum. Multi-year discounts are available — typical commitments are two or three years, with the largest Enterprise deals running five years. Quarterly billing is available on Growth and Enterprise.
What's included in implementation?
Implementation services are scoped separately from platform licensing. Essentials customers typically self-deploy with guided onboarding. Growth and Enterprise customers receive an implementation engagement scoped to the specific module mix, integration count, and user-rollout shape — typically 8 to 14 weeks for a Growth deployment, 10 to 16 weeks for Enterprise.
Do you support single-tenant VPC deployment on Azure as well as AWS?
Yes. The Enterprise tier supports single-tenant VPC deployment on AWS or Azure, with customer-managed encryption keys via AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault. Google Cloud is on the 2027 roadmap.
How do you handle multi-ERP environments in pricing?
Multi-ERP is a first-class concept in the Lattice & Spire data model. Each certified ERP integration counts as one integration against the plan limit. Customers with more than ten ERPs in scope typically land in Enterprise; multi-ERP does not carry a separate surcharge.
Can we start with a single module?
Yes. Many customers start with Supplier 360 and Insights Hub on Essentials, then expand into Risk Radar and Contract Vault as program maturity grows. Modules can be added mid-contract with prorated billing.
Are there discounts for public-sector, non-profit, or academic customers?
We offer a defined public-sector pricing schedule for government, defense (FedRAMP track), and accredited academic institutions. Contact sales for the current schedule and the FedRAMP roadmap.
How do you charge for API usage?
All plans include baseline REST and GraphQL API access for first-party integration. Higher-volume API usage — particularly partner-facing or embedded scenarios — is licensed through the Developer API tier upgrade add-on, with rate-limit and webhook-channel uplifts.
